title: Surjective simplicial abelian-group quasi-isomorphisms fill boundaries
statement: Let $X,Y:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be simplicial abelian groups and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Put $s(X)^{-n}=X_n$ for $n\geq0$, with differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ for $n>0$, and zero positive terms, and define $s(Y)$ similarly. Assume that every homomorphism $f_n:X_n\to Y_n$ is surjective and that $s(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, meaning an isomorphism on all cohomology groups $\ker(d^r)/\operatorname{im}(d^{r-1})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then the underlying simplicial-set map $Uf:UX\to UY$ is a trivial Kan fibration. Explicitly, for every $n\geq0$, every commutative square with left map $\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$ and right map $Uf$ has a simplicial filler making both triangles commute; $n=0$ includes surjectivity on vertices. No multiplicative structure, finiteness assumption, model structure, or topological realization is part of the hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 08P1 (lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups), lines 5837-5881; trivial Kan means the boundary lifting of Definition 08NL.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-normalized-kernel-acyclic] to $f$. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed termwise surjectivity and quasi-isomorphism of $s(f)$. It gives the simplicial kernel $K_m=\ker(f_m)$ and $\ker\partial_m=\operatorname{im}\partial_{m+1}$ in its positive-face normalized complex for every $m\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 08P1 (lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups), second and last proof paragraphs: acyclic kernel and normalization comparison; Homology Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain); Tag 019C (lemma-quasi-isomorphism). Positive-face normalization as in the existing lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence. Returned proof Steps 1-2.

proof.text: Fix a lifting square in dimension $n$. If $n=0$, choose $x\in X_0$ mapping to the vertex $y\in Y_0$, using surjectivity of $f_0$; the boundary is empty. For $n\geq1$, evaluate the lower map $b:\Delta[n]\to UY$ at $\mathrm{id}_{[n]}$ to get $y\in Y_n$, and evaluate the upper map $a$ at the codimension-one injections $\delta_i$ to get $x_i\in X_{n-1}$. Naturality gives $b(\alpha)=Y(\alpha)y$ for every operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, and the lifting square gives $f(x_i)=d_i y$. For $n\geq2$, the face-face identity and naturality of $a$ give $d_i x_j=d_{j-1}x_i$ for $i<j$. For $n=1$ there are no such equations. It suffices to find $x\in X_n$ mapping to $y$ with faces $x_i$; Step 5 checks the whole boundary, including its degenerate simplices.

source.place: Tag 08P1, first proof paragraph; Tag 08NL (definition-trivial-kan); Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), first identity.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ choose $t\in X_n$ with $f(t)=y$ and put $a_i=x_i-d_i t$. Then $f(a_i)=d_i y-d_i f(t)=0$, so $a_i\in K_{n-1}$. When $n\geq2$, the face-face identity gives $d_i a_j=d_i x_j-d_i d_j t=d_{j-1}x_i-d_{j-1}d_i t=d_{j-1}a_i$. Thus $(a_i)$ is a compatible boundary in $K$. A simplex $v\in K_n$ with faces $a_i$ will give $x=t+v$ with $f(x)=y$ and $d_i x=x_i$.

source.place: Tag 08P1, proof, second paragraph: subtract an arbitrary lift of the lower simplex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-normalized-acyclic-compatible-boundary] to $G=K$ and the family $(a_i)$ of Step 3. Step 1 supplies normalized acyclicity, including degree zero; Step 3 supplies every compatibility equation. Obtain $v\in K_n$ with $d_i v=a_i$ for all $i$, also when $n=1$. Hence $x=t+v$ maps to $y$ and has faces $x_i$.

source.place: Tag 08P1 (lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups), third proof paragraph: horn filler and residual normalized cycle, using Tag 08NZ (lemma-simplicial-group-kan). Omit face 0 for the positive-face/d_0 normalization. Returned proof Steps 5-6.

proof.text: Put $x=t+v$ for $n\geq1$, and retain the vertex lift of Step 2 for $n=0$. Define $c:\Delta[n]\to UX$ in degree $m$ by $c(\alpha)=X(\alpha)x$. Functoriality makes this a simplicial map, and naturality of $f$ gives $f(c(\alpha))=Y(\alpha)y=b(\alpha)$. To check the other triangle for $n\geq1$, let $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ be any boundary simplex, so it misses some vertex $i$. The cited face-factorization statement gives $\alpha=\delta_i\circ\psi$. Thus $c(\alpha)=X(\psi)d_i x=X(\psi)x_i=a(\alpha)$ by naturality of $a$. This includes every degenerate boundary simplex. For $n=0$ the boundary triangle is vacuous. Consequently the required fillers exist in all dimensions, which is precisely Definition 08NL of a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Tag 08P1, conclusion, with Tag 08NL (definition-trivial-kan). Factorization is Tag 0166 (lemma-face-degeneracy), as recorded in the cited existing node.

theorem trivialKanFibration_of_surjective_of_quasiIso
    {X Y : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (f.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))))
    (hqis : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      (HomologicalComplex.extendMap
        ((AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map f)
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat.op) n)) :
    SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I.rlp (Functor.whiskerRight f (forget AddCommGrpCat.{u}))

old_proof.text: Let $K_n=\ker(f_n)\subseteq X_n$. Naturality of $f$ restricts every simplicial operator of $X$ to $K$, so $K$ is a simplicial abelian group. The alternating differentials restrict as well. Degreewise surjectivity gives the short exact sequence of cochain complexes $0\to s(K)\to s(X)\xrightarrow{s(f)}s(Y)\to0$, including the zero terms in positive degrees. Apply the cited long exact cohomology sequence. In $H^{r-1}(s(X))\to H^{r-1}(s(Y))\to H^r(s(K))\to H^r(s(X))\to H^r(s(Y))$, the first map is surjective and the last map injective by the quasi-isomorphism hypothesis. Exactness therefore makes the map out of $H^r(s(K))$ both injective and zero. Hence $H^r(s(K))=0$ for every integer $r$.

old_proof.text: Use the positive-face normalization in the cited comparison: $N(K)_0=K_0$, $N(K)_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\ker(d_i)$ for $m>0$, with differential $d_0$. The alternating complex $C(K)$ in that comparison has exactly the terms and differentials of $s(K)$ after replacing chain degree $m$ by cochain degree $-m$. Thus $C(K)$ is acyclic by Step 1. The comparison supplies chain maps $i:N(K)\to C(K)$ and $p:C(K)\to N(K)$ with $pi$ homotopic to the identity. On a cycle $z$, an identity $pi-1=dh+hd$ gives $piz-z=d(hz)$, so $pi$ acts as the identity on homology. The class of $iz$ is zero in $C(K)$, hence $[z]=p_*i_*[z]=0$. This proves that $N(K)$ is acyclic, also in degree zero, whose outgoing differential is zero.

old_proof.text: For $n\geq2$ and $0\leq i\leq n-2$, compatibility for the pair $(0,i+1)$ gives $d_i z_0=d_0 z_{i+1}=0$. Thus all faces of $z_0\in K_{n-1}$ vanish: it belongs to $N(K)_{n-1}$ and is a cycle for $d_0$. For $n=1$, $z_0\in K_0=N(K)_0$ is automatically a cycle. Since Step 2 proved $H_{n-1}(N(K))=0$, the cycle $z_0$ lies in the image of the differential. Choose $w\in N(K)_n$ with $d_0 w=z_0$; the defining kernels give $d_jw=0$ for $1\leq j\leq n$. Therefore $v=u+w\in K_n$ has $d_i v=a_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 08P1, proof, last paragraph: the residual face is a normalized cycle and acyclicity supplies a normalized primitive; using the d_0 convention avoids the last-face sign conversion.

old_proof.text: Put $x=t+u+w$ for $n\geq1$, and retain the vertex lift of Step 3 for $n=0$. Define $c:\Delta[n]\to UX$ in degree $m$ by $c(\alpha)=X(\alpha)x$. Functoriality makes this a simplicial map, and naturality of $f$ gives $f(c(\alpha))=Y(\alpha)y=b(\alpha)$. To check the other triangle for $n\geq1$, let $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ be any boundary simplex, so it misses some vertex $i$. The cited face-factorization statement gives $\alpha=\delta_i\circ\psi$. Thus $c(\alpha)=X(\psi)d_i x=X(\psi)x_i=a(\alpha)$ by naturality of $a$. This includes every degenerate boundary simplex. For $n=0$ the boundary triangle is vacuous. Consequently the required fillers exist in all dimensions, which is precisely the cited definition of a trivial Kan fibration.
